subject: Build the SQL run coordinator: preflight, cross-process user lease, allocation journal, budgets, cancellation and evidence capture before teardown
description:
WHY: the spec's sections on provider choice, run inputs and budgets, and the Preflight…Capture rows of resource lifecycle. Acceptance scenarios "laptop resource pressure" and "actual implementation tests".

FROM TASK 8 (the contract this task produces against; names are final):
- Policy.execution {providers: Id[], budgets: RunBudgets} is required in every Policy. qualification/policy.json holds Loom's initial local values: totalDeadlineSeconds 900, commandDeadlineSeconds 60, engineStartDeadlineSeconds 60, cleanupDeadlineSeconds 60, fixtureFileBytes 2147483648, maxServerMemoryMiB 512, maxDegreeOfParallelism 1, providers ["localdb"]. runChecks must read them, replacing the 900 s per-check default (run.ts:133). A check may declare a stricter command deadline, never a longer one.
- ProviderConfiguration (assurance.schema.json) is the machine-local trusted provider configuration: providersVersion 1, oneOf localdb {id, kind, executable: MachinePath, version} | developer-service {id, kind, serviceName, instanceName, startupChangeAuthorized}. This task decides and documents its file location (outside every repository, never committed). ProviderRef {kind, id} names the selected entry.
- AllocationJournal (journalVersion 1; runId; owner {user: Hash of the OS account, session, process: ProcessIdentity}; provider; phases [{phase: LifecyclePhase, startedAt, finishedAt?}]; resources [{kind: RunResourceKind, identity, path?: MachinePath, process?, state intended|created|removed|residual}]; cleanupClaim?) and RunLease (leaseVersion 1; scope user|machine; holder {process, session}; runId; acquiredAt) are the journal and lease records.
- RunRecord, required now: runVersion, runId, inputDigest (runInputDigest in run.ts), runner, startedAt, finishedAt, revisionSet, checks, evidenceRefs, testOutcome. Optional, for this task to produce: revisionSet.implementation/fixtures/assertions [{path: RelativePath, hash}] and revisionSet.policy {ref, revision, hash}; target {platform: SqlPlatform, capabilities[]}, provider: ProviderRef, engineVersion (database runs only); resourceUsage {peakWorkingSetBytes, diskBytes, phaseDurations [{phase, milliseconds}]} and limits {budgets: RunBudgets, enforcement [{limit: a RunBudgets member name or 'processMemory', enforced, mechanism?}]}, which become required here.
- Typed UNKNOWN: RunRecord.checks[] has optional cause (UnavailableCause: tool-absent, version-policy, unreadable, crashed, timeout, connection, login, cancelled, insufficient-resources, provider-blocked) and dependency (Text). This task gives every UNKNOWN site its cause and dependency: run.ts:116-188 and every runner's outcome('UNKNOWN', …) call, about 95 sites in packages/qualification/src. The generator has no if/then keyword, so "UNKNOWN requires cause" is enforced in code: runChecks refuses to emit an UNKNOWN entry without a cause. Test it, positive and negative.
- QualifyRunStatus.progress.events[] also has an optional cause.

GROUNDING:
- runChecks (run.ts:127) runs checks sequentially (:158). withTimeout is a bare Promise.race (:113-119), and the default deadline is 900 s per check (:133).
- There is no AbortSignal in run.ts, exec.ts or types.ts:60-78.
- exec kills the process tree by pid only (exec.ts:70-84).
- Evidence is written after teardown (run.ts:201-202).
- localdb.ts: create allows 180 s with no explicit version (:42); databases are created without placement or limits (:110-116); a failed create is forgotten (run.ts:97).
- native.test.ts:410 asserts two parallel LocalDB runs.
- sql.json proof limits: only a generic one at :108.
- Host (11:51Z): SqlLocalDB 16.0.1000.6 at Program Files\Microsoft SQL Server\160\Tools\Binn; sqlcmd 15.0.1300.359.

CHANGE (packages/qualification):
- Coordinator phases: preflight, reserve, start, prepare, execute, capture.
  - Preflight covers tool versions, a declared target-capability check against LocalDB's Express-edition limits, free disk, permissions, safe roots and trusted scripts.
- Run inputs: the exact model and import snapshot, implementation files and hashes, target SQL platform, engine version and capabilities, check list, authored fixture set, expected assertions, and the trusted execution policy.
- A per-user OS lease across processes (queued, cancellable), plus a machine lock for a dedicated service. No model write lock is held during native checks.
- A durable allocation journal outside the run directory.
- An explicit LocalDB version.
- Databases are created with ON/LOG ON under the run root and MAXSIZE. max server memory 512 and MAXDOP 1, from qualification/policy.json.
- Budgets:
  - File growth limits are enforced before data loading.
  - Process and disk use are monitored during execution, and peak working set is recorded.
  - A fixture that exceeds the file, memory or deadline budget reports UNKNOWN with cause insufficient-resources and leaves every limit unchanged. One test per budget.
  - An explicit test shows max server memory does not cap every allocation, and records whether OS process limits are enforced.
  - A request for a hard memory guarantee is UNKNOWN with cause insufficient-resources (test).
- AbortSignal through the coordinator, exec, sqlcmd and sessions; abort-and-await replaces the race. Evidence is persisted before teardown.
- RunRecord (decision 10): runChecks now produces resourceUsage and limits for every run, so those fields become required here. provider, engineVersion and target are present for database runs and stay optional. cleanup and outcome become required in task 17, which produces the verified cleanup state.
- Generated DDL fixtures qualify only generated DDL. A negative test shows examples/conforming evidence cannot qualify an adopting implementation.
- Retained capabilities keep named tests: application contract coexistence, and database migration qualification (sql.migration).
- sql.json proof limits: LocalDB evidence cannot establish every Azure SQL or full SQL Server property, nor target-only identity, network or operational evidence.
- native.test.ts:410 becomes "concurrent requests serialize under the lease and each leaves nothing behind".
- Crosswalk: this task co-owns the run-result statement with tasks 8 and 17; record its evidence when the fields it makes required land.

AREA TESTS: npm run build; node --test --test-concurrency=1 packages/qualification/dist/test/framework.test.js; node --test --test-concurrency=1 packages/qualification/dist/test/lifecycle.test.js (new); node --test --test-concurrency=1 --test-name-pattern "catalog|behavior|transaction|migration|operations|connection|serialize" packages/qualification/dist/test/native.test.js. Afterwards `SqlLocalDB info` shows no new loom-* instance.
PRECONDITION: no peer LocalDB run is active (task 1).
WORKER: loom-worker (Sonnet 5, effort high, as its definition sets), resumed across its milestone while its context allows (task 1, warm reuse); Opus at xhigh only through `ledger escalate <task>` when the task proves complex, meaning an unresolved design question or a defect the worker cannot land (owner rule: prefer Sonnet; Opus xhigh only for complex work).
